title: Bad Bunny Rules Monthly Touring Report for Record-Extending 10th Time
summary: Eight shows in Madrid and another handful around Europe did the trick.
contentText:
Bad Bunny wrapped the Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour last night (July 22) in Brussels. But while we wait for final numbers on his last batch of shows, he has another victory to celebrate: He returns to No. 1 on Billboard ’s monthly Top Tours chart for a second time this year, a third time while on this tour, and a record-extending 10th time since the ranking launched in 2019.

According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, Bad Bunny grossed $123.1 million and sold 773,000 tickets across 14 shows during June. That finish falls just short of his own $123.7 million take in September 2022 while on World’s Hottest Tour. He is now the second artist to gross a reported $100 million in two separate calendar months, joining Beyoncé, who has done it six times.

But while he misses his personal-best monthly gross by less than 0.5%, he sets a career best for monthly attendance, surpassing Sept. 22’s 501,000 by 55%. That discrepancy between Bad Bunny’s own history in terms of gross and attendance can be explained mostly by geography: His record revenue from 2022 was bolstered by 11 shows in the United States, where ticket prices outpace the rest of the world, even despite four years of inflation since.

His current, June 2026 routing took him exclusively abroad – eight nights in Madrid, and two apiece in Dusseldorf, Arnhem, and London – where prices are more modest, but stadium capacities are outsized, allowing for giant attendance figures.

Bad Bunny’s decision to not bring his 2025-26 world tour to the United States was a widespread talking point . Here, the results lay bare, as his 2022 tour’s domestic grosses remain his career standard, at least within the limited span of one month compared to another. Overall, however, his international appeal has overcome the lack of U.S. buying power, as the tour’s total gross climbs to $429.7 million through July 5 — already his biggest tour ever by more than $100 million, with six shows left to report.

It’s not just Bad Bunny’s biggest tour, it is the highest-grossing and best-selling tour in Boxscore history to not play any shows in the U.S. (his 31-show residency in San Juan last year is separate from the DTMF World Tour, which kicked off in November). It has also sent his total career grosses beyond $1 billion, making him the first Latin artist ever to gross ten figures.

Bad Bunny previously led the Top Tours chart in December and January, while in Latin America. Earlier, he achieved the tally’s first hat-trick with three consecutive wins on the Most Wanted Tour (2024). In 2022, he was No. 1 for two months while on El Ultimo Tour Del Mundo (Feb. and March,) and another two during World’s Hottest Tour (Aug. and Sept.).

With 10 months at No. 1, Bad Bunny extends his record for the most monthly victories among all artists since the chart’s Feb. 2019 launch. Beyoncé , Coldplay , and Elton John follow with seven each.

Bad Bunny logs four entries on Top Boxscores, including the top spot with his run of shows at Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano. His stay there lasted 10 shows, though only eight were during June. Those grossed $77.3 million and sold 498,000 tickets, but the entire stint earned $96.1 million and sold 623,000 tickets. Even with pro-rated monthly figures, it still leads its closest competition by more than 3:1.

No. 2 on Top Boxscores is courtesy of BTS . Two shows at Riyadh Air Metropolitano grossed $25.1 million on June 26-27, giving the Madrid stadium the top two spots, and making it the month’s biggest venue with $102.3 million.

BTS’ runner-up finish follows two months at No. 1 on both Top Boxscores and Top Tours. On the latter chart, they are No. 6 due to a limited run of just four shows. The group’s other two shows were at home, at Busan’s Busan Asiad Auxiliary Ground on June 12-13. Through the septet’s July 7 performance in London, the Arirang World Tour has grossed $290.9 million and sold 1.6 million tickets so far.

Back on Top Tours, Bad Bunny is followed by Take That , marking the group’s highest appearance ever and fifth time in the top 10. The British boy band grossed $76.7 million and sold 585,000 tickets over 13 shows in June. Previously, it hit as high as No. 5 in April 2019.

Take That’s June run was highlighted by three shows each at Manchester’s Etihad Stadium (June 19-21) and London Stadium (June 25-27). Those stops grossed $20.4 million and $21.5 million, respectively. The entire schedule was confined to the United Kingdom with 10 shows in England, two in Scotland, and one in Wales.

While acts like Metallica , The Weeknd and Linkin Park populate the top 10 with ongoing tours that started as recently as 2024, one artist lands with the first shows of a 2026 jaunt. Ariana Grande is No. 7 with the first batch of dates from the Eternal Sunshine Tour. Between its kickoff on June 6 through a June 30 show in Sunrise, Fla., she grossed $31.2 million and sold 173,000 tickets. Shows continue through Sept. 1 in London.

Stadium season is well underway in Europe and North America, with such shows occupying the entire top 10 of Top Boxscores, and 23 of the top 30 spots. The only arena engagements on the chart are three Sphere stints by Kenny Chesney and No Doubt , plus Grande at Kia Forum and Rüfüs Du Sol at Madison Square Garden.
